newsitem.title: USA: China says will keep inflation below growth rate.
newsitem.headline: China says will keep inflation below growth rate.

text.p: The head of China's central bank on Monday said China would keep a tight enough monetary policy to ensure that inflation stays below the rate of economic growth.
Dai Xianglong, Governor of the People's Bank of China, also reaffirmed that Hong Kong would remain a thriving financial centre after it returns to Beijing rule next July.
"The macro-economic situation in mainland China is steady," he told a meeting on the fringes of the annual meeting of the World Bank and IMF.

"The retail price is expected to rise by about seven percent and is expected to remain steady over the next two years or may even ease further," Dai said, adding growth this year was likely to be nine percent.
Foreign reserves, currently at $90 billion, are likely to reach $95 billion by the end of the year, while external trade has posted some steady growth and the balance of payments is healthy.
"Therefore the exchange rate of the renminbi, which is determined by the market, will remain stable," he added.
M1 money supply growth will be kept at around an annual 18 percent and M2 at 21-23 percent over the next five years, Dai said.
China will also continue reforms to its macro-economic management.

"That is, we will move from reliance on direct control of the volume of credit towards regulating money supply by means of indirect monetary instruments such as reserve requirements, open market operations and interest rate policy," Dai said.
Tight monetary policy will also benefit Hong Kong.
"Those sceptics who have doubted China's commitment to the open-door policy no longer can have doubts after witnessing the implementation of our economic reforms and its achievements," he said.
As China continues its economic reform, Hong Kong's role as an international financial cnetre will become increasingly important.
Hong Kong will host next year's IMF/World Bank meeting.
"(It) will be a magnificent event which commands far-reaching historical significance."
